beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards down. "Let's see what led me to finally have that conversation."

beats.prompt: The past: the big push you and your partner pulled off together.
The present: the quiet that helped you actually see what was uneven.
The future: the honest conversation about the split.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Quiz me. If Justice is about fairness, why did I feel guilty bringing it up, like I was the one doing something wrong?"

options.text: That's the mirror working — looking honestly at yourself doesn't feel comfortable even when you're right.
Feeling guilty means you were actually in the wrong.
Justice shouldn't come with any feelings attached.

elaboration: Justice holds up a mirror to you first, not just the situation — an honest look at yourself was always going to feel uncomfortable, guilt or not.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "He agreed pretty fast, actually. Does that mean the imbalance wasn't as big a deal as I thought?"

options.text: No — it just means balance was overdue on both sides, not only yours.
It means you made the whole thing up.
How fast he agreed doesn't mean anything at all.

elaboration: Cause and effect catching up doesn't need a fight to land — an overdue balance can resolve fast and still have been real.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the push, the quiet that revealed what needed fixing, and the honest account that actually fixed it."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think the hardest part was ever looking at myself in it, not the conversation itself. Feels a lot more even now, actually."
